St Francis Catholic Primary School
Life at St Francis
Welcome to St Francis from the Headteacher
It is a real privilege to be Headteacher of St Francis, a school community that I know and love deeply. At the heart of everything we do is a simple belief: every child deserves to feel known, valued and supported, and to be given the very best opportunities to flourish.
Our vision, “Providing every child with the tools to choose their path to success,” reflects what I want for every child who comes through our doors. Success will look different for each of them, and our role is to help children discover their strengths, develop confidence and resilience, and leave St Francis believing in what they can achieve.
As a Catholic school, our faith and Gospel values shape the way we learn, lead and care for one another. Inclusion is at the heart of St Francis. We are proud of our wonderfully diverse community and are committed to ensuring that every child, whatever their starting point or individual needs, is able to participate fully, feel that they belong and achieve their very best.
We are also a school that loves music! Music is an important part of life at St Francis and something that brings our whole community together. We are very proud of the rich music provision we offer our children, giving them opportunities to sing, perform, learn instruments and experience the joy and confidence that comes from making music together.
I want St Francis to be a school of high expectations and great ambition, but also one filled with kindness, joy, creativity, belonging and love. Academic achievement matters enormously, but so too does developing compassionate, responsible young people who understand that they can make a positive difference in the world.
I believe strongly that children thrive when school, families, parish and community work together. I am incredibly proud to lead St Francis and of the children and staff who make it such a special place.
If you are considering St Francis for your child, I warmly invite you to come and visit us. There is no better way to understand our school than to walk through our doors, meet our children and staff and experience our community for yourself. We would be delighted to welcome you.
Sonia MiguezHeadteacher

Pupil Premium
What is the Pupil Premium
Introduced in 2011, the pupil premium is a sum of money given to schools each year by the Government to improve the attainment of disadvantaged children.
This is based on research showing that children from low income families perform less well at school than their peers.
To view our Pupil Premium report, please visit our Statutory Data page by clicking here
Sports Premium
What is the PE and sport premium for primary schools
Since 2013, the Government have spent millions on improving physical education (PE) and sport in primary schools.
We must use the funding to make additional and sustainable improvements to the quality of physical education (PE), physical activity and sport that we offer.
This means that we use the premium to:
There are 5 key indicators we use to secure improvements:
The engagement of all pupils in regular physical activity – the Chief Medical Officer guidelines recommend that all children and young people aged 5 to 18 engage in at least 60 minutes of physical activity a day, of which 30 minutes should be in school

pageCache.text:
Faith Leaders
Faith Leaders lead acts of worship in classrooms and assemblies and support others to lead worship. Faith Leaders are willing to share their Catholic beliefs with their peers.
The Faith Leaders meet regularly to discuss how they can help others to develop their faith. They plan and deliver Prayer and Liturgy across the school and will talk frequently in assemblies, lead readings at Church and other events/activities that are planned throughout the year.
‘Father, we lift our leaders up to You today. Draw them close to Yourself, Your wisdom, and Your ways through Your grace. Lord, we ask that You would help lead them in making the right decisions that align with what You would like to accomplish in Your will and Your plan. Amen.’
Faith Leaders 2025-2026

pageCache.pageTitle: Fundamental British values - St Francis Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Fundamental British values
The Government set out its definition of British Values in the 2011 Prevent Strategy and these values were reiterated in 2014 by the Prime Minister. The Department for Education reinforced the need ‘to create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values’. These are:
St. Francis Catholic Primary School is committed to serving the community and local area. In so doing, British values are reinforced in the following ways:
Pupils are encouraged to be independent learners, constantly making choices, within a safe and supportive environment. Developing their self-esteem and self-confidence is very important. Pupils are encouraged to understand their personal freedoms and are taught how to use these rights to best effect. All pupils are keen to support charities, whether local, national or global. They are taught consideration for others through the Religious Education curriculum and PSHE lessons in particular. E-safety teaching enables them to make choices in a safe manner.
The importance of laws and rules are consistently reinforced in the classroom, as well as through school assemblies. Pupils are taught to understand the need for laws: that they are there for individual protection, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when laws are broken. Pupils follow a positive behaviour policy and clearly understand the rewards and sanctions that are used. Assemblies and discussions in class focus on recognising right from wrong and visits from the Police and other local community representatives help to reinforce these messages.
Democratic values are an explicit part of the ethos at St. Francis. All adults listen to the views of the pupils and value their opinions. Pupils have further opportunity to have their voices heard through the School Council. The elections of School Council are the result of pupil votes and these groups canvas the opinions of their peers.
The school’s ethos and behaviour policy are based on Gospel values, with the important commandment being, ‘Love one another as I have loved you’. Assemblies constantly promote respect for others and the importance of good manners. All pupils are taught the importance of self-respect, honest and open communication with others and fair play. Pupils work collaboratively and value others’ opinions.
When pupils leave St Francis Catholic Primary School they will:
Tolerance of those of Different Faiths and Beliefs
As a Catholic worshipping community, pupils are reminded of their place in a culturally diverse society. This is achieved through the Religious Education curriculum and the spiritual life of the school. Assemblies and class work promote the diversity of society and the right for each person to be respected and valued equally regardless of ability, gender, faith, heritage or ethnicity.
British Values Statement

pageCache.pageTitle: Worship in School - St Francis Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Worship in School
The school children attend the Parish Mass once a week . Classes attend in rotation with each class from Years 1 to 6 leading a Mass once per term. Masses for the whole school occur on Holidays of Obligation and are celebrated in the Parish Church. Parents and the wider community are invited to attend all Masses. Each classroom has its own prayerful corner and daily prayers are said in the classrooms.
During Assemblies we support the children in discovering their Faith. Liturgical events such as Easter, Christmas, and Holidays of Obligation are celebrated and explained to the children. Current world events are explored. Prayer forms part of each assembly. Themes related to ‘Come and See’ are explored. Successes are celebrated during Friday Merit assemblies.
Each class leads an assembly once a term sharing their work and dedicating prayer, Parents and Carers are invited to attend.

pageCache.pageTitle: Mini Vinnies - St Francis Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Mini Vinnies
Mini Vinnies is a group primary school young people who get together to help those in need within their school and local community. Mini Vinnies introduces children to social justice issues and to living faith through action as part of the St Vincent de Paul Society.
The St Vincent de Paul Society is a lay Catholic organization that aspires to live the gospel message by serving Christ in the poor with love, respect, justice, hope and joy, and to bring about a more just and compassionate society.
We follow the motto of the Mini Vinnie logo, to ‘turn concern into action’.
‘Lord Jesus, you made yourself poor, so help us give our hearts to the poor and help us to see God in their eyes. Help us to see that they are just like you; hungry, lonely and going through hard times. Please help the family of St Vincent de Paul to not be boastful, to live simply and to be united.’

pageCache.pageTitle: About - St Francis Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
About
St Francis Catholic Primary School exists to help the parents of this area to bring up their children in the Catholic Faith in the context of a good education. It is central to our mission that every child matters as a unique gift from God. As a Christian community we aim to develop the whole child within an ethos of faith, love, care and respect.
Our mission is to provide high quality:
The school is commissioned to do this by the Trustees of the Catholic Archdiocese of Southwark in the parish of Peckham in partnership with the Local Authority, Southwark.
St. Francis Catholic Primary School is a two form entry primary school. The new building was built in 1970 on a site adjacent to the original St Francis School, which was a four storey Victorian building.
The school is set in pleasant grounds which consist of gardens and three playgrounds – KS2, KS1 & Nursery.
In the immediate vicinity are many Local Authority Housing estates and small local shops.
The majority of pupils at St. Francis are members of the parish of Our Lady of Sorrows, Peckham. The children are Catholic and have one or both parents supporting their faith. We have a small number of Christian children from other denominations.
At present the gender mix in school is almost equal. There are slightly more girls than boys. We have a wide cultural mix, with many children of African origin, some children of Caribbean descent and a number of South American, European and British families.
Children start the main school in Reception, during the year in which they are 5. Each September thereafter the children move to the next class in Years 1 through to 6 – this numbering system forms part of the structure of the National Curriculum. When a child completes Year 6 at St Francis they will join a secondary school for Year 7.
St. Francis Catholic Primary School has a one form entry Nursery which admits twenty-five children during the year in which they are 4.
